title: Move cfile.h to epan/libwireshark
description:
cfile.h includes a bunch of headers from epan/. Thus, it can't be
put into the main set of includes always installed without creating
some potential issues for any system that tries to install only
the development headers for libwsutil (and possibly libwiretap).

cfile.h also includes a header from wiretap, and (implicitly,
some made explicit here) headers from wsutil. cfile.h is included
by a file from libuiqt-plugin. libwireshark already depends on
libwiretap and libwsutil, and libuiqt-plugin already depends on
libwireshark, so moving it to epan is the correct answer to ensure
that we have a DAG.

Ping #20901

AI-Assisted: no

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • 7304d571 - Move cfile.h to epan/libwireshark
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/24552/diffs?diff_id=1763729819&start_sha=8f3f26a16be4f42717d747917d4f4a65c507b719)

Moving the header to epan is I think clearly correct. The question is whether to move `cfile.c` to epan as well. If we do that, then `cap_file_init` has to be made WS_DLL_PUBLIC. That seems fine if the struct is public.

Then there's all the file packet provider functions that are not visible. `file_packet_provider.c` doesn't need to go into `epan`, but then again those functions probably don't need to be in the public header, and could be moved to `file.h` or a new `file_packet_provider.h` file in the root directory and not shipped as public headers.

added 1 commit
  • 4ebe1aea - Also move cfile.c to epan
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/24552/diffs?diff_id=1763775333&start_sha=7304d571a21e2ad6ba1c7695f680a8cc62a05d31)

The current CMakeLists.txt has

```
# sources common for wireshark, tshark, rawshark and sharkd
add_library(shark_common OBJECT
	cfile.c
	extcap_parser.c
	file_packet_provider.c
	sync_pipe_write.c
)
```

(that comment should be fixed to mention the stratos as well; I'll do that).

That's somewhat of a mixed bag of source files. Which of them belong in, say, libwireshark, which of them belong in some other existing library, and which of them belong in shark_common?

Of those:

`sync_pipe_write.c` is used by `capture_sync.c`. There's a `capchild` static library which is built which includes that; it should probably be moved into the `capture/` directory and add to that. The executables that need it are the ones that already link with `capchild` and also dumpcap, which links in a special way.

`file_packet_provider.c` could also be moved into `libwireshark`; it can't go anywhere else (but it could stay.) Move it to `libwireshark` if we want to make it easier for people to develop other applications like `sharkd` or whatever that use capture files in some fashion.

That would leave `extcap_parser.c`, along with `extcap.c`, which are the files in the root directory that are used by applications that use extcaps. That's separate from the files in the `extcap/` directory, which are extcaps themselves plus some necessary files for building your own extcaps. The latter should probably be some kind of shared `libextcap` directory or something so that people can build their own extcaps out of tree. We could move the application-using-extcap files in there too, against if we want to make it easier for people to develop their own applications that use extcaps.
